clue.text: Very fast job, as the reformation

parts.note: a post is a job or position

indicators.note: a reformation reshapes something, so the letters of 'as the' are formed again in a new order

explanation.surface: A quick job description, with a sideways nod to the speed of the Protestant Reformation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the reformation' looks like the historical event; here it is a verb-like signal acting on the words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Posthaste is an old adverb for something done with great speed, as by post riders.

clue.text: Section is said to be calm

indicators.note: 'is said' tells us the word for calm is heard spoken, not spelt

parts.note: peace is a state of calm

explanation.surface: Someone describing a quiet part of a building or a piece of music as calm.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece is a portion or part of something, so it is a synonym for a section.

clue.text: Tramples family member

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read as two words
second meaning: a partner's son from an earlier relationship

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer after STEPS and it becomes a verb phrase meaning tramples.
explanation.definitionFit: A stepson is a partner's son from an earlier relationship, a relative by marriage.

clue.text: One may laugh and laugh about desire

indicators.note: 'about' means the laugh goes around the word for desire

parts.note: HA is the sound of a laugh
a yen is a longing or desire

explanation.surface: A cheerful thought that someone might laugh and keep laughing over something they want.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter uses 'laugh' twice on purpose: once in the definition, once as the wordplay's sound of laughter.
explanation.definitionFit: The spotted hyena is known for its cackling call, often called laughing.

clue.text: School briefly covers up conspiracy smear

indicators.note: 'covers up' means the school abbreviation sits around the conspiracy, hiding it

parts.note: SCH is a short form of school
a plot is a secret plan or conspiracy

explanation.surface: A school hushes up a conspiracy to smear someone's name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smear' looks like slander but here it is a dirty mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A splotch is a messy stain or blot, the kind of mark a smear leaves.

clue.text: Bizarre report of former lover, silly cretin

indicators.note: a report is what is heard, so the word for former lover is taken by its sound

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: 'silly' suggests the letters of cretin are jumbled into a foolish order

explanation.surface: Someone calls an old flame a silly cretin and is told that is bizarre.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, EX sounds like the opening ECC of the answer; 'silly' turns CRETIN into ENTRIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Eccentric means odd or unconventional, close in sense to strange or weird.

clue.text: See 26
Mr Bloggs introducing the start of your free pleasure trip

indicators.note: 'introducing' means the name takes the other letters into its middle

parts.note: Joe Bloggs is the British name for an average person

indicators.note: 'the start of' means only the first letter of your is used

parts.note: to rid is to free or clear

explanation.surface: An everyman takes you for a free outing.
explanation.walkthrough: Joe Bloggs is the British equivalent of John Doe, a name for an ordinary person.
explanation.definitionFit: A joyride is a drive taken for fun, often in a stolen car, so a trip for thrills.

clue.text: Gloomy nature's in fashion

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape, so these letters are shaped into a new word

explanation.surface: A remark that nature is in vogue, or that nature's style is gloomy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in fashion' looks like a phrase meaning trendy; 'in' is part of the letters and 'fashion' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturnine describes a sullen, morose temperament, linked in old astrology to the planet Saturn.

clue.text: Sexual and genuine after breaking even

indicators.note: 'after' puts the word for genuine after the rearranged letters
'breaking' means the word even is broken and rebuilt in another order

parts.note: real means genuine

explanation.surface: Something sexual and authentic once a tie or deadlock is broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking even' reads like a business phrase; EVEN rearranges to VENE.
explanation.definitionFit: Venereal relates to sexual intercourse, chiefly in the phrase venereal disease.

clue.text: Reserved hotel inside for Wile Ethelbert?

parts.note: coy means shy or reserved

indicators.note: 'inside' means only the inner letters of hotel are kept

explanation.surface: A shy guest booked into a hotel for someone called Wile Ethelbert.
explanation.walkthrough: The cartoon character is Wile E. Coyote; his middle initial was once given as Ethelbert. 'hotel inside' gives OTE.
explanation.definitionFit: The full name of the Road Runner cartoon predator is Wile E. Coyote, so the question mark marks a definition by example.

clue.text: Praise revolutionary Iran once

indicators.note: 'revolutionary' says the letters of praise turn over into a new order

explanation.surface: Praise for Iran's revolution of 1979.
explanation.definitionFit: Persia was the country's official name in the West until 1935.

clue.text: More appetising with or without first sip of sherry or port

parts.note: tangier means having a sharper, more appetising flavour

indicators.note: 'first sip of' means just the opening letter of sherry

explanation.surface: A wine buff wonders whether sherry or port tastes better with or without a first sip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the drink; it is a harbour city. The city is spelt Tangier or Tangiers, hence 'with or without' the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Tangiers is the Moroccan harbour city on the Strait of Gibraltar, a well-known seaport.

clue.text: Trousers needing inch off, so sent back

indicators.note: 'off' says the letters of inch are wrong, so they are put in a new order
'sent back' means the word so is read backwards

explanation.surface: Trousers being returned to the shop because they need taking up an inch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inch off' sounds like tailoring; INCH rearranges to CHIN, and SO backwards is OS.
explanation.definitionFit: Chinos are casual trousers made of a cotton twill fabric.

clue.text: Vacating house before nuclear meltdown is very hard

indicators.note: 'before' puts those letters ahead of the rest
a vacated house is emptied, leaving only its first and last letters
a meltdown wrecks the word nuclear, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Getting out of a house ahead of a nuclear meltdown would be very hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Herculean, from the labours of Hercules, describes a task needing enormous effort.

clue.text: Political figure, one from 20?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a senior and respected politician
second meaning: 20 is AMERICA, so one from the States

explanation.walkthrough: The answer to 20 is AMERICA, often called the States; split the word to get a man from there.
explanation.definitionFit: A statesman is an experienced, respected leader in public affairs, a leading politician.

clue.text: The woman's satisfied if coming first, being completely tight

parts.note: her refers to a woman; the 's is read as 'has'
to have met a demand is to have satisfied it

indicators.note: 'first' asks for the opening letters of if and coming, the words before it

explanation.surface: A woman is pleased if she comes first, being thoroughly drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming first' looks like part of the story but picks the first letters of 'if' and 'coming', giving IC.
explanation.definitionFit: A hermetic seal is airtight, closed so nothing can pass in or out.

clue.text: Declare it's proper to drink cola, shaken or stirred

indicators.note: 'to drink' means the prim word takes in the other letters, swallowing them

parts.note: prim means stiffly proper

indicators.note: 'shaken or stirred' says the letters of cola are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone announcing that it is quite proper to drink cola, mixed like a cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shaken or stirred' nods to James Bond's martini order.
explanation.definitionFit: To proclaim is to announce publicly and officially, much like a formal declaration.

clue.text: Leaves trendy gold jewellery at last

parts.note: chic means stylish and trendy
or is gold in heraldry

indicators.note: 'at last' means only the final letter of jewellery

explanation.surface: Someone walks out wearing fashionable gold jewellery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb meaning departs; it is a noun, salad leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicory is a plant whose bitter leaves are eaten in salads.

clue.text: Belligerent mother's on trial when leader demoted

parts.note: ma is mother; the 's is read as 'is'

indicators.note: the leading letter of trial is demoted, moving down one place

explanation.surface: A mother is in court, and the lead defendant has been demoted.
explanation.walkthrough: The T at the head of TRIAL drops one place to give RTIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Martial relates to war and fighting, so it suits an aggressive, warlike stance.

clue.text: Cold alleviated and stopped

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
eased means alleviated or relieved

explanation.surface: A cold got better and then went away.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceased is the past tense of cease, meaning came to an end or halted.

clue.text: Continent of Asia has heart ripped out by organised crime

indicators.note: 'by' makes the crime the agent that fills the hole left in Asia, so it goes inside
with its heart ripped out, Asia keeps only its outer letters, and the gap is filled
'organised' says the letters of crime are put in a new order

explanation.surface: The heart of Asia is torn apart by organised crime.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as crime destroying a region; in the wordplay the rearranged crime simply fills the gap where the heart was.
explanation.definitionFit: America names a continent, either North or South, or the two Americas taken together.

clue.text: Rebel sounds quiet between these walls

indicators.note: 'sounds' tells us the phrase is heard aloud rather than read

parts.note: quiet is mute, and between these walls is in here, making MUTE IN HERE

explanation.surface: A prisoner keeping his rebellious thoughts hushed inside these walls.
explanation.definitionFit: A mutineer is someone who rises against authority, especially on a ship, so a rebel.

clue.text: Continue working after brief look back

indicators.note: 'after' puts the word for working at the end
'back' means the word for a brief look is read backwards

parts.note: a peek is a quick look
on means working, as a machine is on

explanation.surface: A worker carries on after a quick glance over the shoulder.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep on is to carry on or persist with something, a phrasal verb for persisting.

clue.text: They say you might need this to start the engine in the shade

indicators.note: 'they say' means the item is named by how it sounds

parts.words: you might need this to start the engine
parts.note: you start a car's engine with a car key

explanation.surface: Someone needing their key to start a car parked in the shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the shade' looks like a place to park; 'shade' is a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Khaki is a dull brownish-yellow colour, best known from army uniforms.

clue.text: Times (long and short) come up with a letter

indicators.note: in a down answer 'come up' means the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: an age is a long time
a mo is a short time, a moment

explanation.surface: A newspaper's long and short pieces arrive alongside a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: AGE is a long time and MO a short one; reversed they make the letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the last character of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Measure for Measure partly correct

indicators.note: partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's Measure for Measure is partly right.
explanation.definitionFit: To reform is to amend or put right, so it fits correct as a verb.

clue.text: Philistine's with a drink, exhausted, drained and unreal

parts.note: Philistine is the setter, so Philistine's is I'm
gin is a drink

indicators.note: 'drained' empties exhausted of its middle, leaving its first and last letters

explanation.surface: The setter, worn out after a drink, feels everything is unreal.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's name is Philistine, so 'Philistine's' means 'I'm', IM.
explanation.definitionFit: Imagined means existing only in the mind, so not real.

clue.text: Merely, purely, barely

parts.note: only means merely
just means simply or purely

explanation.surface: A list of three adverbs of limitation.
explanation.definitionFit: Only just means by the narrowest margin, hardly at all, a common idiom.

clue.text: For a start, looks like new au pair's out, one being childless

indicators.note: 'out' means the letters are out of place and must be rearranged
'For a start' takes the opening letters of looks, like and new

parts.note: pair, with the 's read as 'is'

explanation.surface: It looks as though the new au pair has left a family with no children to mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'au pair' reads as one person, but its two words go into the mix as letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Nullipara is the medical term for a woman who has never given birth.
